attrs.mechanism: Agent hypothesis. Add a zero-initialized learnable feature vector g to each arm. Keep the incumbent output intact, then add 0.1 × tanh(g) × compressed_current in the candidate. The generated control adds 0.1 × tanh(g) × compressed_preceding_context only where a predecessor exists. Both use the same parameter count, initialization, coefficient, and final valid-token mask. Zero initialization makes each arm equal the incumbent before learning; a nonuniform gain distinguishes current-state calibration from context calibration.

attrs.claim: The negative aggregate and mixed direct-versus-state contrast are compatible with no incremental benefit from explicit item identity, sufficient identity in the incumbent, optimization or capacity effects shared by both arms, unequal source-tensor distributions despite normalization, changed gradients to the shared item embedding, or seed, checkpoint, and category variation. The historical local-difference failure is context, not replication of this mechanism.
